resources.string: Add Matter devices to Home Assistant
Your phone lends its Bluetooth to Home Assistant for a moment. Home Assistant does the actual pairing, and the device stays in your own network.
No Google services, no cloud, no tracking
Credentials stay encrypted on this phone
Works with the Matter Server app 9 and newer
Used when you are not at home
This address is not encrypted. That is common inside your home network, but use HTTPS for external access.
Enter a full address starting with http:// or https://

No Home Assistant found at this address. Also tried:
%1$s

Check the address and that the phone is on the same network.
Recommended. Your password is only entered on your own Home Assistant page.
Create one under Profile → Security in Home Assistant.
Adding devices needs an administrator account.
The server uses a certificate that this phone does not trust (for example a self-signed one). Only continue if this fingerprint matches the one of your Home Assistant:\n\n%1$s
Scan the code on the device. Wi-Fi and Thread devices are both supported.
Already set up with another app or hub? Add it here too, over the network.
Find the Matter QR code on the device, its packaging or manual
You can also hold an NFC tag to the phone
Camera access is needed to scan. You can also type the code.
No Matter QR code found in this picture.
The 11- or 21-digit number next to the QR code
This is not a Matter code.
This QR code is damaged or not a Matter code.
A setup code has 11 or 21 digits.
The setup code contains only digits.
This code has a typo. Check the digits again.
This code is not valid for Matter.
This code uses an unsupported format.
This device has to be prepared in the manufacturer\'s app first. Open that app, put the device into pairing mode, then come back.
Put the device into pairing mode now, usually by holding its button for a few seconds.
Making sure everything is set for pairing
Phone can act as Bluetooth proxy
Battery optimisation may stop pairing when the screen turns off.
On mobile data the phone may lose Home Assistant during pairing.
Only needed for Thread devices: set a preferred Thread network in Home Assistant (Settings → Thread) with an online border router.
Only needed for Wi-Fi devices, once: store your 2.4 GHz network so Home Assistant can pass it on. Thread devices do not need it.
Home Assistant has its own Bluetooth adapters or proxies. If one of them sees the device first, it is used instead of this phone.
Weak signal. Move closer to the device.
Not found yet. Make sure the device is powered and in pairing mode.
Install and start the Matter Server app (version 9 or newer) in Home Assistant.
The Matter Server app needs the option \"ble_proxy\" to use this phone.
%1$d devices match this manual code. Keep only the one you want to add in pairing mode, or scan the QR code instead.
%1$d other Matter devices are in pairing mode nearby.
This sets \"ble_proxy\" in the Matter Server app and restarts it. Matter devices are unavailable for a few seconds.
Matter Wi-Fi devices only use 2.4 GHz. The details are stored in Home Assistant\'s Matter server, not on this phone.
Only needed for Wi-Fi devices, and only once. Thread devices do not need it, so you can skip this.
Many routers have a Wi-Fi QR code on a sticker. Another phone can show one under Settings → Wi-Fi → your network → Share.
No Wi-Fi QR code found in this picture.
Network name and password taken from the QR code.
Android only shows the name of your current network to apps with location permission. It is used for nothing else.
Your phone is on 5 GHz right now. Matter devices need 2.4 GHz, so make sure this network also offers 2.4 GHz.
Thread network handed to the Matter server
Keep your phone near the device
Waiting for the previous attempt to end…
Weak signal (%1$d dBm). Move closer to the device.
Another Bluetooth proxy seems to have taken over the device. This can take longer or fail. Turn off nearby ESPHome proxies for a moment if it does.
The phone switched to mobile data. Stay on Wi-Fi until pairing is done.
The Bluetooth connection is closed right away. You can try again without resetting the device.
Your Home Assistant user is not an administrator.
The Matter Server app was not found or is not running.
The phone could not connect as Bluetooth proxy. Check that \"ble_proxy\" is enabled in the Matter Server app.
Another Bluetooth proxy took over the device and did not finish.
The device could not be verified as a certified Matter device.
The device didn\'t come online in your network.

• Put the device into pairing mode (often: hold the button 5–10 s)
• Pairing mode usually ends after 15 minutes, so power the device off and on again
• If it was paired before, reset it to factory settings
• Check that the code belongs to this device
• Temporarily turn off ESPHome Bluetooth proxies near the device\n• Or disable Bluetooth on the Home Assistant host for a moment\n• Then try again with the phone close to the device
• Move closer to the device\n• Turn Bluetooth off and on again\n• Try again
• Check the code (scan the QR code if possible)\n• The device may already be paired with another system: reset it to factory settings
• Test or developer devices need \"enable_test_net_dcl\" in the Matter Server app options
• Thread: a preferred Thread network with an online border router is needed\n• Wi-Fi: the device only supports 2.4 GHz networks\n• Check the list on the previous screen
• Open the check list and use \"Fix\" next to BLE proxy
• Try again\n• Share diagnostics if the problem persists
It\'s now available in Home Assistant.
Home Assistant is still setting up the device. You can name it later in Home Assistant.
The device is removed from Home Assistant. To use it again you may need to reset it.
Scan this code in the other app within 3 minutes. The device stays in Home Assistant.
In the other app (e.g. a hub or a manufacturer app) choose \"Share\" or \"Connect to other service\". It shows a new code. Scan or enter that code here. No Bluetooth needed.
